plan.contextChunk: This figure is an annotated graph of one full cycle of a transformed sine wave, marked up to expose its midline, amplitude, and period. The vertical y-axis carries ticks from -2 up to 4, the horizontal x-axis is labeled at pi/2 and at pi, and both axes end in arrowheads. The solid dark blue curve leaves the y-axis at height 1, rises to a maximum of 4 a quarter of the way along, falls back through that starting height, bottoms out at -2 near three-quarters of the way, and returns to height 1 at pi. A horizontal orange arrow at the level y = 1 extends rightward from the vertical axis, labeled Midline: y = 1. A vertical teal arrow runs up the curve's peak from that orange level to the maximum, tagged by a leader with Amplitude: |A| = 3. Below the plot, a red double-headed arrow spans the width of the drawn cycle beneath the label Period = pi. The three annotations measure independent things: the vertical center of the oscillation, the stretch away from that center, and the horizontal distance before the shape repeats. Taken together they are the quantities needed to reconstruct the equation of a sinusoid from its picture alone.

interactionPlan.concept: A sinusoidal wave can be fully described by its midline (vertical center), amplitude (maximum vertical distance from the midline), and period (horizontal length of one full cycle).
elements: x-axis with right-pointing arrowhead and tick marks at intervals of π/2
y-axis with top and bottom arrowheads and tick marks at integer values
solid dark blue sine wave curve
orange horizontal arrow starting from the y-axis, indicating the midline, with dynamic label 'Midline: y = ...'
teal vertical arrow pointing from the midline to the first peak, with dynamic label 'Amplitude: |A| = ...'
red horizontal double-headed arrow placed below the plot spanning exactly one cycle, with dynamic label 'Period = ...'

interactions.label: Amplitude
interactions.teaches: Amplitude stretches the wave vertically away from the midline; it does not change the wave's vertical center.

interactions.label: Midline
interactions.teaches: The midline shifts the entire wave up or down, acting as the new horizontal center of oscillation.

interactions.label: Period (multiples of π)
interactions.teaches: Period compresses or stretches the wave horizontally, changing the distance required to complete one full cycle.

demo_steps.title: Base parameters
demo_steps.narration: This sine wave is visually characterized by three independent properties: where it is vertically centered, how tall it grows, and how wide one cycle is.

demo_steps.title: Shift the midline
demo_steps.narration: Changing the midline moves the entire graph up or down without altering its overall shape or height.

demo_steps.title: Change the amplitude
demo_steps.narration: Changing the amplitude stretches the wave vertically from the midline, making the peaks higher and the troughs deeper.

demo_steps.title: Adjust the period
demo_steps.narration: Stretching the period makes the wave wider, increasing the horizontal distance needed to complete one full repeat.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Amplitude, midline, and period visually separate into vertical stretch, vertical shift, and horizontal stretch, which map directly to the parameters in a trigonometric equation.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Plot a sine wave y = A*sin(2*pi/P * x) + D based on the slider values. Format x-axis tick labels as fractions of π. The orange midline should be drawn as a horizontal arrow from x=0 to the end of the first cycle. The teal amplitude arrow must extend exactly from the midline to the first peak. The red period marker should be a double-headed arrow spanning from x=0 to x=P placed neatly below the x-axis, with its text label centered. Update all annotation labels dynamically as sliders change.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for amplitude: the learner drags the teal amplitude handle from the midline to the peak, the peak and trough move farther from or closer to y = 1, and the update shows amplitude as vertical distance from the midline.
- Slider for midline: the learner drags the orange midline arrow up or down, the entire sine wave shifts with it while its height from midline to peak stays fixed, making vertical shift separate from amplitude.
- Slider for period: the learner stretches or compresses the red period span, the wave completes one cycle over the new horizontal distance, showing period as repeat length rather than wave height.

authoredContext:
Inspecting the graph, we can determine that the period is π, the midline is y=1, and the amplitude is 3. See the figure.

A graph of y=3sin(2x)+1. The graph has an amplitude of 3. There is a midline at y=1. There is a period of pi. Local maximum at (pi/4, 4) and local minimum at (3pi/4, -2).

discrepancies: The generated chart includes full gridlines across the plot area, whereas the source figure only uses tick marks on the axes
The generated plot shows a much wider coordinate domain and range than the source, making the central annotated cycle appear smaller and introducing extra repetitions of the wave
The source uses a leader line for the Amplitude label to place it in empty space, while the generated label is placed directly next to the arrow, causing it to overlap the sine wave
The sine wave in the source has arrowheads at its left and right terminal ends, which are missing in the generation
The Period double-ended arrow and label are placed far down at y = -4.5 rather than just below the bottom of the y-axis
evaluation.notes: Excellent interactive implementation that brings the static concepts to life with a step-by-step player and sliders, though the default visual styling (unnecessary gridlines, wide view crop) departs slightly from the original textbook aesthetic.
action_items: Set 'drawOnChartArea: false' in the grid options for both scales to remove the inner gridlines while keeping the axis tick marks
Crop the initial view closer to the source by reducing the x-axis domain (e.g., -0.5 to 4) and y-axis range (e.g., -3 to 5)
Adjust the custom annotations to draw a thin leader line for the Amplitude label so the text can sit cleanly to the right without overlapping the curve
Draw arrowheads at the start and end coordinates of the sine wave dataset to match the source figure
Move the Period annotation vertically closer to the bottom of the graph (e.g., y = -2.5) rather than pinning it to the bottom of the wide viewport

feedback.rationale: Scores are exceptionally high with no failure modes, and the action items are minor styling and layout adjustments, indicating the figure is good enough to stop iterating.
